newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends flat on market liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends flat on market liquidity.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed unchanged on Friday at 21.25 percent after a volatile session in which ample liquidity offset pressures from a weaker peso, traders said.
"Inflation figures and a sagging peso hit overnight rates early on, but they calmed down in later trade and settled down at average trading rates for recent sessions," one trader said.
Overnight Cetes rates had reached a session high of 22.30 percent in early trade.
In late trade on Thursday, Banco de Mexico announced Jan 1-15 consumer inflation was 1.6 percent, compared to an average forecast of 1.24 percent in a Reuters survey.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 2.05 centavos weaker at 7.8150/7.8175 per dollar.
"The inflation figures were not good, but the secondary market is still awash with liquidity, so they just curbed the downward trend in rates," a dealer said.
Banco de Mexico drained surplus liquidity of 332 million pesos from the system through an auction to purchase paper, which it assigned overnight at a rate of 22.75 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile fell 10 basis points to close at 23.25 percent.
Dealers saw primary rates bucking a recent downward trend to increase slightly at next week's central bank auction.
"The peso is under pressure and primaries have come down enough already, so we expect increases, albeit slight ones," a dealer said.
Bellwether 28-day primary Cetes (Treasury Certificates) rates currently stand at 22.93 percent.
Dealers said that recent primary rate falls could be reined in by recent volatility in U.S. long bond yields ahead of the Feb 4 Federal Open market Committee Meeting to review U.S. interest rates.
Liquidity of 332 million pesos is expected to flow back into the system on Monday, when Friday's central bank auction to drain a market surplus falls due.
